<details>

<summary>Init.lua</summary>

```lua
---@diagnostic disable: undefined-global
local function setup_deps(path_to_site)
  local mini_path = path_to_site .. "pack/deps/start/mini.nvim"
  if not vim.uv.fs_stat(mini_path) then
    vim.cmd('echo "Installing `mini.nvim`" | redraw')
    vim.fn.system({ "git", "clone", "--filter=blob:none", "https://github.com/echasnovski/mini.nvim", mini_path })
    vim.cmd("packadd mini.nvim | helptags ALL")
    vim.cmd('echo "Installed `mini.nvim`" | redraw')
  end
  require("mini.deps").setup({ path = { package = path_to_site } })
end
setup_deps(vim.fn.stdpath("data") .. "/site/")

local function setup_mini_autocompletion()
  require("mini.snippets").setup() -- only using lsp snippets...
  require("mini.completion").setup({ lsp_completion = { auto_setup = false, source_func = "omnifunc" } })
end

local function custom_on_attach(bufnr) vim.bo[bufnr].omnifunc = "v:lua.MiniCompletion.completefunc_lsp" end

vim.o.completeopt = "menuone,noselect,fuzzy"
vim.o.shortmess = "CFOSWaco"
vim.g.mapleader = " "
MiniDeps.now(function()
  require("mini.notify").setup()

  setup_mini_autocompletion()

  MiniDeps.add("neovim/nvim-lspconfig")
  vim.api.nvim_create_autocmd("LspAttach", {
    group = vim.api.nvim_create_augroup("my.lsp", {}),
    callback = function(args) custom_on_attach(args.buf) end,
  })
  vim.lsp.enable("rust_analyzer")
end)
```

</details>

<details>

<summary>Example code(rust)</summary>

```rust
trait State {}

struct Dummy<State> {
    d1: u32,
    // d2:
}

fn main() {
    println!("Hello world!");
}
```
</details>


Sometimes, using provided `fuzzy` matching does not result in optimal code completion.
In the video above, I am adding `PhantomData<State>` to the line containing `// d2:`.

As demonstrated, I need to type `State` completely before it shows at the top of the completion list. Apparently, `State` is a word used often inside core rust libraries ...)

The fuzzy-matching [part](https://github.com/Saghen/blink.cmp/blob/f233029f79312d1028cbf168a8eef3182bac5a4f/lua/blink/cmp/fuzzy/init.lua#L63) of `blink.cmp` uses a `frecency` and `proximity` bonus. As such, `State` becomes first in the completion list when I type `S`.

I want to keep using `mini.completion` and wrote some [code](https://github.com/abeldekat/nvim_pde/blob/603c86b11188a9605e7acbdfeb9b52429c8bc868/lua/ak/mini/completion_blinked.lua#L1) to bridge `mini` with `blink.cmp`. The core idea is to override [process_items](https://github.com/echasnovski/mini.nvim/blob/088d67751584e4168f35bca89bad70ada7ea4636/doc/mini-completion.txt#L266), providing a custom function for [opts.filtersort](https://github.com/echasnovski/mini.nvim/blob/088d67751584e4168f35bca89bad70ada7ea4636/doc/mini-completion.txt#L375).

I am [using](https://github.com/abeldekat/nvim_pde/blob/603c86b11188a9605e7acbdfeb9b52429c8bc868/lua/ak/config/coding/mini_completion.lua#L77) blink's fuzzy in the following way:

```lua
-- ...
if Util.mini_completion_fuzzy_provider == "blink" then
  require("ak.mini.completion_blinked").setup()
  opts.lsp_completion.process_items = function(items, base)
    local opts = { filtersort = CompletionBlinked.fuzzy }
    return MiniCompletion.default_process_items(items, base, opts)
  end
end
require("mini.completion").setup(opts)
-- ...

```

comment_data.body:
> Sometimes, using provided `fuzzy` matching does not result in optimal code completion. In the video above, I am adding `PhantomData<State>` to the line containing `// d2:`.
> 
> As demonstrated, I need to type `State` completely before it shows at the top of the completion list. Apparently, `State` is a word used often inside core rust libraries ...)

Yes, this is because there is a high bonus in built-in Vim's fuzzy matching for camel case word start. It also seems to favor matches at the end and not the start.

This was addressed in neovim/neovim#32953, which unfortunately is a Neovim>=0.12 only. So `filtersort` with `vim.fn.matchfuzzy(items, base, { camelcase = false })` should behave more reasonable here. So something like this:

```lua
local lsp_get_filterword = function(x) return x.filterText or x.label end
local filtersort = function(items, base)
  if base == '' then return vim.deepcopy(items) end
  return vim.fn.matchfuzzy(items, base, { text_cb = lsp_get_filterword, camelcase = false })
end
local process_opts = { filtersort = filtersort }
local process_items = function(items, base) return MiniCompletion.default_process_items(items, base, process_opts) end
require('mini.completion').setup({ lsp_completion = { process_items = process_items } })
```

The problem with using this as default is because it will work only if LSP server always returns `isIncomplete = true`, in which case `process_items` will be responsible for filtering and sorting after each key press. Some (most?) servers might return `isIncomplete = false` when there all possible candidates are returned. In this case built-in fuzzy matching takes over and it will sort similar to `camelcase = true`, which will be not quite intuitive.

Unfortunately, currently there is no way to tweak built-in fuzzy completion behavior (beyond just enabling that). Maybe @glepnir can help with that :eyes:?

reply_data.body:
> [vim/vim@9d2b727](https://github.com/vim/vim/commit/9d2b7275589bd3f712debdb2f5b0468ce160f415) This commit implements a new algorithm. Continuous matches from the beginning with more than three scores will exceed the camelback. But I finally withdrew this default behavior. Recently I'm thinking that maybe I should add it back.

I was thinking more about the possible ways for the user to control fuzzy matching in the "true" ins-completion-menu. For example, with 'completeopt=menuone,fuzzy' pressing `<C-n>` will still have high preference for camel case at the end instead of start. And as far as I understand, there is no way for user to control that, right?

> Emm, what is the effect of `isInComplete`? This means that the current result is incomplete. Subsequent input will still send a completion request and get the result. So you can get the current prefix and then fuzzy it with the new result?

That's more a 'mini.completion' thing. For `isIncomplete = true` it is possible to adjust `camelcase = false` behavior after the next key press, because indeed fuzzy matching will eventually go through `vim.fn.matchfuzzy()`. But for `isIncomplete = false` the next key press will use built-in fuzzy matching (as this is more performant and less code in 'mini.completion') which can not be adjusted to have `camelcase = false` like behavior.

comment_data.body:
The latest `main` (after a9e4cb303ea6269ecab92c0276baf9d04370c492) should now work better in this case. Only on Neovim>=0.12, I am afraid, as it introduced `camelcase = false`. Plus there is also a [suggestion to add "nosort" in 'completeopt' together with "fuzzy"](https://github.com/echasnovski/mini.nvim/blob/a9e4cb303ea6269ecab92c0276baf9d04370c492/doc/mini-completion.txt#L88-L89). Thanks @glepnir for the hint!

I think the initial reason for this "Show and tell" should be resolved, but this might still benefit from being open as it has non-trivial set up for using custom fuzzy matching algorithm. Although I do indeed find it perplexing to have two completion engines installed and used.

title: [mini.completion] Fuzzy matching with blink.cmp algorithm
